description_full: Paychex, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides human capital management solutions (HCM) for human resources, payroll processing, employee benefits, and insurance services for small to medium-sized businesses in the United States, Europe, Canada, India, and Israel. It offers technology and advisory solutions; and payroll tax administration services. The company also provides retirement solutions, such as plan implementation, ongoing compliance with government regulations, employee and employer reporting, participant and employer online access, electronic funds transfer, and other administrative services; HCM solutions from recruiting and hiring to retirement; and talent management and talent acquisition services. In addition, it offers payroll solutions, including calculation, preparation, and delivery of employee payroll checks; production of internal accounting records and management reports; preparation of federal, state, and local payroll tax returns; and collection and remittance of clients' payroll obligations. Further, the company provides workforce management solutions; benefits administration solutions; digital marketplace for earned wages, financial wellness solutions, and voluntary lifestyle benefits; administrative services organization HR outsourcing solutions; solutions to payroll and non-payroll customers; retirement and funding solutions; and insurance services for property and casualty coverage, such as workers' compensation, business-owner policies, cyber security protection, and commercial auto, as well as health and benefits coverage, including health, dental, vision, and life. Additionally, it offers payroll, HR, employee benefits administration, retirement, insurance, risk management outsourcing, and access to professionally trained HR representatives, virtually and on-site. It markets and sells its solutions primarily through its direct sales force. Paychex, Inc. was founded in 1971 and is headquartered in Rochester, New York.

financial_summary: Paychex, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $40.1B market cap on $6.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 52% against a 9% cost of capital — a 44-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $2.3B in free cash flow — roughly 36 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.45× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 9.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 10% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 39% operating margin runs 32pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.65x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 0.1% of sector revenue and 0.2% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-6.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 535 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 7% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 8% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 12% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 31% and a beta of 0.79, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.11 vs 5y 0.76), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $305.5M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 44% in the 2020 crash, 23% in the 2022 bear market and 43% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 5% below its DCF fair value of $119, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 22%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $90.98 to $162 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/FCF 17.3 vs 23.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 13% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.8% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 5.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The 15 covering analysts target $115 on average, 2% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 52% clears the cost of capital of 8.6% by 44pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.18).
It converts 36% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.45x.
ROE of 47% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (4.3x equity multiplier).
It spends 1.5% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.2x net debt to EBITDA ($1.1B of cash against $4.6B of debt), with interest covered 9.3x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.2% over 3 years, 9.9% over 5 years and 8.2% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 15.2% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (3.6% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 44, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
Analysts expect 7.2% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 10.2%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 85%.
It returns 5.5% a year to shareholders (1.5% in buybacks and 4.2% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 37 consecutive years, raising it 11.8% a year over the last five.
people: With about 17,600 employees, each generates about $370K of revenue, in line with the Technology median, and revenue has grown 7.7% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $132K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.8M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
